The reader misread the hint: app-bar line 22 is Logout, not 'Account Settings'. The bar is hidden on /signup anyway. But the signup submit (signup.component.ts:48) dispatches Signup. After HTTP success (auth.state.ts:183-184) this runs ReceiveAPIAccessToken, which dispatches Navigate([redirect || '/']). redirect is the URL AuthGuard captured: MustLogin(state.url) at auth.guard.ts:18, which keeps the query string, fragment and matrix parameters. It survives the move from /login to /signup. Example: a signed-out user opens /projects?x=1 or /user-settings#a, is sent to /login, clicks Sign up and signs up. The app then calls router.navigate(['/projects?x=1']). Angular splits a single string command only on '/', so it becomes one literal segment 'projects?x=1'. No route matches it, so the root '**' route redirects to /404 (app.module.ts:61-62). So /404 is reached only through redirectTo. This relies on @angular/router 12's createUrlTree treating the string literally. node_modules is not installed, so that is standard Angular behaviour, not code in the repository. It is an edge path, but a real one.

Clicking Sign in on /login calls login() (component.ts:53), which runs historyService.goToPreviousState('workloads') after the HTTP login succeeds. That calls navigateByUrl(previousStateUrl_) (history.ts:52). previousStateUrl_ comes from the pairwise NavigationEnd tracker (history.ts:36). Example: a user on /search?q=x signs out from the chrome user panel (authService.logout navigates to /login), or a 401 makes error/handler.ts:57 navigate to /login. Logging back in then goes to /search?q=x. Correction to the reader's mechanism: AuthGuard.pushState sets previousStateUrl_ equal to currentStateUrl_ (extractedUrl.toString() equals initialUrl.toString() under the default UrlHandlingStrategy), so that path falls back to 'workloads'. The verdict still holds through the history path. The chrome search form itself is not shown on /login.

The reader's reason is wrong, but the verdict holds. A sender does exist: DefaultSyncService sends 'convertAccountToKeyConnector' (libs/common/src/platform/sync/default-sync.service.ts:290), and submit on this screen runs loginSuccessHandlerService.run, which does a fullSync. After that, submit navigates to /vault, where authGuard can redirect to /remove-password (auth.guard.ts:108). Both paths require convertAccountRequired$, which needs loggedInUsingSso = tokenService.getIsExternal. /device-verification exists only in a master-password login: it is reached only from LoginComponent (login.component.ts:445), and only PasswordLoginStrategy implements logInNewDeviceVerification. So that condition stays false on this screen and no trigger shown here can reach /remove-password. Caveat: this rests on the client treating the token's 'external' amr as an SSO login; the server that issues the token is not in the repository.

The reader's claim of 'no sender' is false. DefaultSyncService sends 'convertAccountToKeyConnector' after any sync for which convertAccountRequired$ is true (libs/common/src/platform/sync/default-sync.service.ts:290). AppComponent, shown on every screen, handles it with router.navigate(['/remove-password']). On this screen the user can trigger a sync: the Purge vault button opens PurgeVaultComponent, which calls fullSync(true) (src/app/vault/settings/purge-vault.component.ts:65). A server-notification sync can also fire here. In addition, the product switcher's /vault link runs UserLayout's authGuard, which redirects to /remove-password under the same condition (auth.guard.ts:108). The condition depends on backend data that can change during the session: an SSO login plus non-admin membership in a Key Connector org.

On self-hosted installs, the org layout's upgrade callout calls upgrade(), which navigates to /settings/subscription/premium. The premium badge in the vault-item dialog (no org id) also reaches the same route through web-premium-upgrade-prompt.service.ts:99.

The AppComponent 'upgradeOrganization' handler is the only hinted trigger. That message is sent only from vault screens (vault-cipher-actions.service.ts:123 and individual vault.component.ts:934). recover-delete is an anon screen that offers only routerLink /login, a submit that navigates to '/' (which goes on to /login for a signed-out user), and the environment selector. Nothing shown on it can send that message or reach org billing.

The callout's upgrade() opens UnifiedUpgradeDialog, which contains app-upgrade-payment. When the Families plan is chosen and the user owns a free org, that step shows a routerLink to `/organizations/${org.id}/billing/subscription` (upgrade-payment.service.ts:76-82).
